name: CaptionFlow
requirements: After Effects CC or newer, Windows or macOS
titleSeo: CaptionFlow — Free After Effects SRT Caption Script
descriptionSeo: Free After Effects script that imports SRT subtitle files as timed text layers. Sentence or word-by-word modes, built-in caption editor, optional punctuation removal. Works with Arabic text.
tagline: Turn any SRT subtitle file into timed, stylable After Effects text layers in one click.
summary: CaptionFlow imports an .srt subtitle file and lays every subtitle block into your composition as a live text layer, already trimmed to its timecode. No copy-pasting timings by hand, no third-party caption plugins.
Because the result is ordinary text layers, everything stays editable: your fonts, animation presets, masks, and motion graphics tools all work on the captions. What you render is what you styled.

Two import modes cover the two caption styles editors actually use. Sentence mode creates one layer per subtitle block, the standard for readable talking-head captions. Word-by-word mode creates one layer per block entry, for karaoke and pop-style kinetic captions.

features.title: SRT import with timing
features.text: Each subtitle block becomes a text layer with its in and out points set from the SRT timecodes. Nothing to re-time by hand.

features.title: Sentence or word-by-word
features.text: One layer per subtitle block for standard captions, or split entries for word-pop and karaoke-style kinetic captions.

features.title: Built-in caption editor
features.text: A dialog lists every caption block with its text and timecodes. Fix a typo or nudge an in/out point, then apply the changes back to the layers.

features.title: Punctuation removal
features.text: One checkbox strips periods, commas, question marks, and quotes for a cleaner social-caption look.

features.title: Dockable panel
features.text: Installs as a ScriptUI panel, so it lives in the Window menu next to your other workspace panels.

install: Close After Effects, then copy the file into the ScriptUI Panels folder: on Windows, C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe After Effects <version>\Support Files\Scripts\ScriptUI Panels. On macOS, Applications, Adobe After Effects <version>, Scripts, ScriptUI Panels.
Relaunch After Effects and open the panel from the Window menu (listed as CaptionFlow by ishoil).
In Preferences, under Scripting and Expressions, enable "Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network" so the file dialog works.
usage: Select the composition where the captions belong and set the work area to the video length.
In the Import section pick the mode: Sentence / Phrase or Word by Word.
Press Import SRT File, choose your .srt, and the text layers are created with timing applied.
Use Open Caption Editor to review every block, fix text, and adjust in/out timecodes, then apply.

faq.a: Yes. Free for personal and commercial projects. A credit or a link back to this page is appreciated but not required.

faq.q: Which After Effects versions are supported?
faq.a: Any CC release and newer. The script is written in ExtendScript and runs on Windows and macOS.

faq.q: Does it work with Arabic subtitles?
faq.a: Yes. CaptionFlow creates standard text layers, and Arabic text works once the layer uses an Arabic-capable text engine and font. For splitting Arabic text per word, see the Text Burst tool on this site.

faq.q: Does it burn the captions into the video?
faq.a: It creates live text layers, not a burned render. You style and animate them like any text, and they render as part of your composition.

faq.q: Can I fix timing mistakes in the SRT?
faq.a: Yes. The built-in caption editor shows every block with its timecodes; edit the in/out fields and apply the changes.

ar.title: سكربت CaptionFlow لتحويل ملفات ترجمة SRT إلى طبقات نص في أفتر إفكت
ar.description: سكربت مجاني لأدوبي أفتر إفكت يستورد ملف ترجمة SRT ويحوّله إلى طبقات نصوص مضبوطة التوقيت داخل الكومبوزيشن، مع محرر ترجمة مدمج وخيار إزالة علامات الترقيم. يدعم النصوص العربية.

name: Text Burst
requirements: After Effects CC or newer, Windows or macOS
titleSeo: Text Burst — Split After Effects Text Layers per Word or Character
descriptionSeo: Free After Effects script that splits any text layer into one layer per character, word, or line. Optional expression link, Arabic RTL support, dockable panel.
tagline: Split one text layer into one layer per character, word, or line, ready to animate.
summary: Kinetic typography means animating pieces of text separately, and doing that by hand means duplicating layers and retyping fragments all day. Text Burst does the split in one click: pick the layer, choose the granularity, done.
The split works per character, per word, or per line, so the same tool covers letter-pop animations, word-by-word reveals, and line-by-line editorial motion.

Two modes control how the pieces relate to the source. With expressions, each fragment stays linked to the original text, so fixing a typo updates every layer. Without expressions, you get plain baked layers with nothing extra attached.

features.title: Character, word, or line
features.text: One dropdown chooses the split granularity for any selected text layer.

features.title: Expression link or baked layers
features.text: Keep fragments synced to the source text through expressions, or output plain independent layers.

features.title: Arabic RTL support
features.text: A language toggle handles right-to-left text correctly, so Arabic splits into properly ordered layers.

features.title: Dockable panel
features.text: Installs as a ScriptUI panel in the Window menu like any native workspace panel.

install: Close After Effects, then copy the file into the ScriptUI Panels folder: on Windows, C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe After Effects <version>\Support Files\Scripts\ScriptUI Panels. On macOS, Applications, Adobe After Effects <version>, Scripts, ScriptUI Panels.
Relaunch After Effects and open the panel from the Window menu (listed as Text Burst by ishoil).
usage: Create one text layer with the full line you want to animate.
Select it, then choose the split: characters, words, or lines.
Pick the mode: with expressions to stay synced to the source, or without for baked layers.
Press go. Each fragment arrives as its own layer, trimmed and positioned, ready for your animation presets.

faq.a: Yes. Free for personal and commercial projects. A credit or a link back to this page is appreciated but not required.

faq.q: Which After Effects versions are supported?
faq.a: Any CC release and newer, on Windows and macOS.
Yes. The language toggle enables right-to-left handling, so Arabic text splits into correctly ordered layers.

faq.q: What is the difference between the two modes?
faq.a: With expressions, fragments reference the original layer, so editing the source text updates them. Without expressions, each fragment is a plain, independent layer.
